title: ChatGPT-Based Simulation Helps to Develop the Pre-Service Mathematics Teachers’ Critical Thinking
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT can be used as a simulation tool in mathematics teacher education and whether working with ChatGPT-generated solutions can develop pre-service teachers’ critical thinking. The authors frame ChatGPT as a digital platform that can imitate pupils’ responses in school mathematics, including plausible but incorrect reasoning, and ask whether pre-service teachers can identify and correct such errors.

The intervention was a pedagogical experiment conducted at Sumy State Pedagogical University in Ukraine with 32 pre-service mathematics teachers: 14 bachelor’s students and 18 master’s students. Participants worked with ChatGPT on problems involving mathematical induction, first analyzing generated proofs, then identifying and correcting mistakes, and finally requesting alternative solution methods. Their performance was scored across four indicators related to critical thinking, and the same task was repeated a month later to assess change.

The authors report that ChatGPT frequently produced incorrect or incomplete mathematical reasoning, which made it useful as a simulation of student work. Participants were generally able to detect errors, though some tasks—especially correcting ChatGPT’s mistakes and evaluating alternative methods—were challenging. A Wilcoxon test comparing the two rounds showed improvement over time, leading the authors to conclude that using ChatGPT in this simulation format can support the development of pre-service mathematics teachers’ critical thinking. However, the findings are limited to one institution, one topic, a small sample, and a short intervention period.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a small single-site pedagogical experiment with pre/post pairwise comparison and no control group, so it provides only limited causal evidence. The study is peer-reviewed, but internal validity is constrained by small sample size, topic-specific tasks, and potential practice effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The observed gains in critical thinking are positive but modest and reported only for a specialized pre-service teacher sample, not a general K-12 student population. No effect size was reported, and the main result is a localized training outcome rather than broad educational impact.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as a math-problem answering simulator for secondary school pupils in pre-service mathematics teacher training, generating correct and incorrect solution attempts that students must analyze, debug, and correct.
ChatGPT-based simulation of quasi-professional classroom practice, where pre-service teachers inspect AI-generated pupil answers and practice error detection and correction.

finding.finding_summary: The study reports that repeated work with ChatGPT-generated math solutions improved pre-service mathematics teachers' critical thinking. Using a paired design with n=32 and a one-sided Wilcoxon test, the authors report T=243 and reject the null hypothesis; 18 of 22 students with changed scores improved on the second assessment.
finding.measure: Critical thinking task scores based on four indicators: critical analysis of information, identifying logical inconsistencies, rectifying inconsistencies, and selecting the most rational problem-solving approach
